A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HTC-VLM and are readable throughout, including figures, equations, tables, and supplementary material. Much of v1's supplementary Sections 7–13 is incorporated into v2's Sections 5–6, allowing additions to be distinguished from relocations.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original HTC-VLM benchmark results, representation probing, and ablations. These establish original empirical results despite some supplementary tables being explicitly marked as placeholders.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark and probing results and adds reported experiments on Qwen-VL-Chat and LLaVA-NeXT in Section 6.6 and Table 8.

M1.justification: The reported default mask changes from isolating visual tokens to allowing intra-visual attention while blocking text access to raw visual tokens (Equation 6 and Algorithm 3). The discrete projector changes from 14112→8192→4096 to 14112→16384→4×4096. Four semantic anchors were already present in v1; the changes concern the masking procedure and projector specification.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven primary benchmarks plus TextVQA and MMVet, with the same stated training-data setup. The added backbone experiments reuse existing benchmark coverage; higher-resolution encoders and AnyRes concern model and input-processing settings rather than a new dataset, population, or task.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain Q-Former, average pooling, VoCo-LLaMA, ToMe, FastV, PDrop, and SparseVLM in their respective experiments. The new backbone comparison reuses Vanilla and VoCo-LLaMA. The two masking variants remain represented, although their proposed-method and ablation roles change.

E3.justification: Section 6.6 adds evaluations on Qwen-VL-Chat and LLaVA-NeXT, including their higher-resolution and dynamic-resolution processing, without hyperparameter retuning. Table 8 specifies macro retention as Method/Vanilla for these new comparisons. Reported projector capacities also change, including the default from 149M to 500M parameters; the original optimization settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a cross-architecture generalization stress test and substantially revises the masking analysis: visual isolation becomes the stricter ablation against a default permitting visual interaction. Most other studies—including codebook, loss-weight, projector, anchor-count, fusion, probing, and attention analyses—already appeared in v1, often in its supplementary material.

E5.justification: Both versions state that throughput is averaged over 500 runs. Neither reports experimental random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The retained variance comment concerns hyperparameter sensitivity rather than repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: New Table 8 reports HTC-VLM retention of 94.5% and 95.7% on Qwen-VL-Chat and LLaVA-NeXT, versus 86.4% and 86.6% for VoCo-LLaMA under those settings. The original 87.2% versus 81.0% headline remains unchanged. Other revisions include ToMe's 192-token GQA score from 52.4 to 54.3, corrected Q-Former/pooling retention entries, HTC-VLM summary latency from 54 to 61 ms, revised ablation retention summaries, and the reversed mask ranking. The earlier latency figures were marked provisional, so these are reporting revisions rather than established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: v1 contains information-bottleneck equations and references to theorems and an absent proof section. v2 adds explicit assumptions, a notation table, and proof arguments for entropy domination and a tighter hybrid ELBO in Section 5.3. It also removes the earlier star-graph attention factorization while retaining much of the relocated theoretical rationale.

C1.justification: The central hybrid-compression contribution and 87.2% headline remain. v2 narrows the state-of-the-art claim to the evaluated one-token baselines and newly foregrounds cross-backbone generalization and formal theoretical analysis in its contribution list.

C2.justification: The masking explanation reverses: v1 attributes poorer visual mixing to oversmoothing, whereas v2 argues that isolation harms spatial and anchor–patch context. Efficiency discussion changes from effectively no overhead to an explicit semantic-encoder cost that parallel execution may only partly hide. v2 also qualifies advantages over moderate-budget pruning and adds encoder-cost and dense-localization limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public-code availability statement and repository link. It revises projector dimensions, parameter counts, and mask-construction pseudocode. Most reproducibility information—including optimizer, batch size, learning rate, hardware, and approximately 90 GPU-hours—was already supplied in v1 and remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 cites its conference version and explicitly positions itself as a journal extension. It adds works such as CF-VLM and TransHP and replaces the survey cited for MME with the MME benchmark paper. The main related-work categories and positioning against continuous compression, quantization, and pruning remain.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the document by integrating supplementary theory, implementation, and analyses before the conclusion. It removes the supplementary overview, expands the contribution and extension narrative, and rewrites masking, efficiency, and conclusion passages. The title and author information change, and author biographies are added.

P2.justification: The document adopts a journal layout with a full-width abstract, different typography, resized and relocated figures, and extensively reformatted tables. New displays include the notation and cross-backbone tables plus author portraits. The four research figures largely reuse existing content rather than introduce new visual evidence.

improvement.justification: The cross-backbone comparisons, corrected baseline entries, clearer organization, and more candid efficiency discussion offer benefits. However, v2 reverses the central mask-ablation finding without explaining the revision, and identical codebook values change from explicitly provisional in v1 Table 8 to measured in v2 Table 10 without documenting that transition. These unresolved issues in the basis and consistency of the empirical evidence prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
